open_points.subject: OwnerFormField concrete field contract
open_points.question: Must State 6 adopt these three fields exactly, or may it choose another concrete shape that represents the same three facts?
options: Adopt the three candidate fields exactly.
Use different field names while preserving all three facts.
Use a nested or discriminated representation that preserves all three facts.
consequences: Exact adoption gives every generated consumer the same field names and types.
Renaming requires all contracts and consumers to use the selected names consistently.
Nesting or discrimination changes construction and access patterns while retaining the model's meaning.
open_points.requirement: Facts: the field's name; whether it belongs to the request or to its values; how its text is read.

open_points.subject: OwnerFormCarrier and FormValueKind definitions
open_points.question: What concrete variants and serialized values must OwnerFormCarrier and FormValueKind use?
options: Define enums with two carrier variants and four value-kind variants.
Define discriminated literal unions with those semantic alternatives.
Use validated strings constrained to those alternatives.
consequences: Enums provide named members that consumers may import and compare directly.
Literal unions keep the alternatives in the field type without runtime enum objects.
Validated strings reduce type dependencies but require explicit validation and canonical spelling choices.
open_points.requirement: A row of the owner form table: one field of the owner's pages — what the owner types or picks in a form — as the owner interface names it on the page and reads it back (owner, 2026-11-25): its name, whether it belongs to the owner's request itself or to the values the owner gives, and how its text is read: as text, as a whole number, as yes or no, or as one of a closed list.
open_points.default_guess: Define enums whose carrier variants mean request and values and whose value-kind variants mean text, whole number, yes or no, and closed list.

set_aside.subject: OwnerFormField table availability
set_aside.text: The release: the owner form table the data provider holds.
set_aside.question: Must the product expose the owner form table to another module or caller, or may it remain unused/internal release data?
options: Require a read operation that returns the release's owner form table.
Require the table only as an internal release constant, with no public operation.
Do not require the product to make the table available in this release.
consequences: A read operation creates a required result whose completeness and refusal behaviour State 2 must define before State 5 can contract it.
An internal constant requires no caller-facing operation but still needs module ownership and any direct import edges.
No availability requirement permits generation to omit all behaviour involving OwnerFormField.
set_aside.requirement: A row of the owner form table: one field of the owner's pages — what the owner types or picks in a form — as the owner interface names it on the page and reads it back (owner, 2026-11-25): its name, whether it belongs to the owner's request itself or to the values the owner gives, and how its text is read: as text, as a whole number, as yes or no, or as one of a closed list.
set_aside.default_guess: Require a read-only operation returning the complete release table.
set_aside.set_aside_because: an unchanged passage of a unit reviewed for its change

set_aside.subject: OwnerFormField module ownership and boundary surface
set_aside.text: The release: the owner form table the data provider holds.
set_aside.question: Which module owns OwnerFormField and, if another module reads the table, which provider operation or exported constant supplies it and what result, failures and effects may the consumer rely on?
options: The models module owns and exports OwnerFormField, while a release-catalog provider owns a read operation returning the table.
A release-catalog module owns both OwnerFormField and the read operation.
The models module owns OwnerFormField and exports the table directly as a release constant.
OwnerFormField remains private to the data-provider module and no other module imports it.
set_aside.default_guess: Place OwnerFormField in models and give a release-catalog provider a side-effect-free operation returning the complete table.
